terms.comment: Classically “shut up, enclose”; Traupman’s word for closing a file.

phrases.latin: Cum autem redieritis, jānua mea clausa erit; nōlī intrāre, nisi avia tēcum veniet.
phrases.english: But when you come back, my door will be shut; don’t come in unless Grandma comes with you.
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
